content.text: Dupuytren contracture is a benign, insidious overproduction of fibrous tissue within the palmar fascia. Tissue knots form under the skin and eventually create a thick cord that can bend the finger(s) into a flexed position.

Despite the name 'contracture,' this condition does NOT involve muscle, tendons, or neuromuscular dysfunction. The affected tissue is the palmar fascia only — it is not an inflammatory condition and is not a painful condition.
Primarily affects older people of European descent, with people assigned male at birth more commonly affected. Occurs more commonly in people with diabetes mellitus or long-term alcohol consumption.

items: Difficulty extending the finger(s)
Difficulty using a keyboard
Inability to flatten the palm (e.g. push-ups or donning gloves)

content.text: It is a slowly progressive condition. Usually starts unilateral but can become bilateral. The 5-year recurrence rate is nearly 50% even after successful treatment.

content.text: The Bunnel-Littler test can help: if MCP extension increases with DIP and PIP flexion, the long finger flexors are limiting ROM and Dupuytren contracture is confirmed. If no change, an MCP capsular restriction is present.
Dupuytren contracture is a long-term, progressive condition that is highly resistant to treatment or change. Even after successful treatment (e.g. surgery), there is a 50% 5-year recurrence rate.

content.title: Cautions
content.text: Do not force the joints beyond their range in extension. Long, gentle stretching is more effective than deep stretching or aggressive tissue mobilisation.
Dupuytren's is resistant to change. Short-term improvements (minutes to hours) in mobility may be experienced, but resolution of the complaint will not occur.
It is a progressive, long-term condition. Frequent treatments to help promote and preserve available function are recommended.

quiz.question: Dupuytren contracture involves muscle tissue and neuromuscular dysfunction.
quiz.explanation: Dupuytren contracture affects the palmar fascia ONLY — it does not involve muscle, tendons, or neuromuscular dysfunction.

quiz.question: What is the 5-year recurrence rate of Dupuytren contracture after successful surgery?
quiz.explanation: Even after successful treatment (e.g. surgery), there is a 50% 5-year recurrence rate.

quiz.question: Which digits does Dupuytren contracture most commonly affect?
quiz.explanation: Dupuytren most commonly affects the fascia in line with digits 3-5.
